about: Massachusetts's inner borders, town by town: scripts/ma-shapes.mjs reads this, gives every town to a shetach and writes data/shapes/ma-*.geojson (which data/shetachim.json claims), along the real town lines (owner, Nov 3: "Look at the North Shore. That's like a proper, nice European border type" — not smoothed curves, "so ugly and unsettling"), except where a town line made a spike or a zigzag: there a straight line between two town corners cuts across (`cuts`; owner: "Straight can also work sometimes ... a hybrid of straight and not straight"). Change a town here, then run `node scripts/ma-shapes.mjs` and `npm run build`. Towns not listed go by their middle's longitude: west of `deren` is Connecticut's shetach (its own band claim, kept exact), between `deren` and `split` Central Massachusetts, east of `split` Eastern Massachusetts. A cut's towns are split along its line: left of it (drawn from its first point to its second) to `left`, the rest to `right`. Cape Cod and the Islands keep their three counties exactly. `exact`: shetachim that keep their own town (and tract) claims in shetachim.json (the North Shore); the shapes are cut to them.

cuts.why: Prus–Fogelman: Wellesley's corner poked east and Dover west, a zigzag; one nearly vertical line instead, from the Weston/Wellesley/Newton corner down to Medfield's corner on Dover (owner, Nov 3: "there are many sections that it can just be a vertical line"). Wellesley Weston Chabad House stays Fogelman's, Needham's Chabad Prus's.

Prus–Fogelman: Sharon and Foxborough's line made a double spike; a straight line from the Walpole/Foxborough/Sharon corner to the Sharon/Mansfield/Easton corner. Sharon's two houses stay Prus's, Mansfield's Fogelman's.
Merrimack Valley–Prus: Wilmington's thin prong up into Andover; a straight line across its base, from the Tewksbury/Wilmington/Andover corner to the Andover/North Reading/Wilmington corner.
